      children: "### Use component\n\n```html app.component.html\n<!-- app.component.html -->\n<fieldset>\n\t<legend>Checkbox group example</legend>\n\t@for (checkboxName of checkboxNames; track checkboxName) {\n\t<db-checkbox\n\t\t(change)=\"checkbox = checkboxName\"\n\t\t[label]=\"'Checkbox ' + checkboxName\"\n\t\t[value]=\"checkboxName\"\n\t\tname=\"CheckboxGroup\"\n\t></db-checkbox>\n\t}\n</fieldset>\n```\n\n```ts app.component.ts\n// app.component.ts\nimport { Component } from \"@angular/core\";\n\n@Component({\n\tselector: \"app-app\",\n\ttemplateUrl: \"./app.component.html\"\n})\nexport class AppComponent {\n\tcheckboxNames = [\"X\", \"Y\", \"Z\"];\n\tcheckbox = \"\";\n}\n```\n\n#### Adding Formatted Infotext\n\nThe message property of the db-checkbox does not accept HTML content for security reasons (to prevent XSS attacks). To add a richly formatted description, use the `db-infotext` component as a sibling element. You must link both components using the [`aria-describedby`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-describedby)-HTML-attribute to ensure accessibility.\n\n```html\n<db-checkbox aria-describedby=\"checkbox-message\">\n\tExample Checkbox\n</db-checkbox>\n<db-infotext id=\"checkbox-message\"> Example <strong>Text</strong> </db-infotext>\n```\n\n```ts app.component.ts\nimport { Component } from \"@angular/core\";\nimport { DBCheckbox, DBInfotext } from \"@db-ux/ngx-core-components\";\n\n@Component({\n\tselector: \"app-root\",\n\tstandalone: true,\n\timports: [DBCheckbox, DBInfotext],\n\ttemplateUrl: \"./app.component.html\"\n})\nexport class AppComponent {}\n```\n\n### How to use with Signal Forms\n\n[Angular Signal Forms](https://angular.dev/essentials/signal-forms) (Angular ≥ 21) are supported via Duck-Typing. The `DBCheckbox` component exposes a `checked` ModelSignal that Angular's `[formField]` directive recognizes automatically as a `FormCheckboxControl`.\n\n```ts app.component.ts\n//app.component.ts\nimport { DBCheckbox } from '@db-ux/ngx-core-components';\nimport { FormField } from '@angular/forms/signals';\n\n@Component({\n\t// ...\n\timports: [\n\t\t// ...,\n\t\tDBCheckbox,\n\t\tFormField\n\t],\n\t// ...\n})\n```\n\n```ts form.component.ts\n// form.component.ts\nimport { Component, signal } from \"@angular/core\";\nimport { form } from \"@angular/forms/signals\";\n\nexport class FormComponent {\n\tmodel = signal({ acceptTerms: false });\n\tmyForm = form(this.model);\n\n\tonFormSubmit(): void {\n\t\talert(JSON.stringify(this.model()));\n\t}\n}\n```\n\n```html form.component.html\n<!-- form.component.html -->\n<form (submit)=\"onFormSubmit()\">\n\t<db-checkbox\n\t\tlabel=\"Accept Terms\"\n\t\t[formField]=\"myForm.acceptTerms\"\n\t></db-checkbox>\n\t<button type=\"submit\">Submit</button>\n</form>\n\n<h2>Output</h2>\n<dl>\n\t<dt>checkbox's value</dt>\n\t<dd>checkbox {{ myForm.acceptTerms().value() ? \"\" : \"un\" }}checked</dd>\n</dl>\n```\n\n#### Controlling validation timing\n\nBy default, Signal Forms validation errors appear immediately. To show errors only after user interaction, use a helper method with the `[validation]` property:\n\n```typescript\nimport { type FieldTree } from \"@angular/forms/signals\";\n\nfieldValidation<T>(field: FieldTree<T>): \"invalid\" | \"valid\" | \"no-validation\" {\n  if (field().dirty() && field().invalid() && !field().pending()) return \"invalid\";\n  if (field().dirty() && field().valid() && !field().pending()) return \"valid\";\n  return \"no-validation\";\n}\n```\n\n```html\n<db-checkbox\n\tlabel=\"Accept Terms\"\n\t[formField]=\"myForm.acceptTerms\"\n\t[validation]=\"fieldValidation(myForm.acceptTerms)\"\n></db-checkbox>\n```\n\n#### Invalid message fallback cascade\n\nWhen a form field becomes invalid, the displayed error message is resolved through the following priority chain (first match wins):\n\n1. **`invalidMessage` prop** — explicitly set on the component\n2. **Signal Forms schema message** — `errors[0].message` from the form schema validators\n3. **Browser default** — native `validationMessage` (e.g. \"Please check this box if you want to proceed\" for `required`)\n4. **`\"TODO: Add an invalidMessage\"`** — fallback indicating a custom message should be provided\n\n### How to use with Template Driven Forms\n\nThird party controls require a `ControlValueAccessor` to function with angular forms. Adding an `ngDefaultControl` attribute will allow them to use that directive.\n[Further information](https://stackoverflow.com/a/46465959)\n\n```ts app.component.ts\n//app.component.ts\nimport { FormsModule } from '@angular/forms';\n\n@Component({\n\t// ...\n\timports: [\n\t\t// ...,\n\t\tFormsModule\n\t],\n\t// ...\n})\n```\n\n```html form.component.html\n<!-- form.component.html -->\n<form>\n\t<db-checkbox\n\t\t(change)=\"checkbox = $event.target.checked\"\n\t\tname=\"checkbox\"\n\t\tlabel=\"Checkbox\"\n\t></db-checkbox>\n\t<db-button type=\"button\" variant=\"brand\" (click)=\"showValues()\"\n\t\t>Get checkbox value</db-button\n\t>\n</form>\n\n<h2>Output</h2>\n<dl>\n\t<dt>checkbox's value</dt>\n\t<dd>checkbox {{ checkbox ? \"\" : \"un\" }}checked</dd>\n</dl>\n```\n\n```ts form.component.ts\n// form.component.ts\nexport class FormComponent {\n\tcheckbox = \"\";\n\tshowValues(): void {\n\t\talert(JSON.stringify({ checkbox: this.checkbox }));\n\t}\n}\n```\n\n### How to use with Reactive Forms\n\ncoming soon … if your interested in contributing, you're very welcome ;)"
